Assignment: AdaBoost for Regression

SOLUTION (instructor copy)

The problem

A small data set has one input \(x\) and a numeric response \(y\):

\(x\) 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
\(y\) 2 5 5 5 7 6 10 9

You will build an AdaBoost.R2 model with three regression stumps, using

  • square loss: \(L_i = \left(\dfrac{|y_i-\hat y_i|}{D}\right)^2\) where \(D=\max_i|y_i-\hat y_i|\)
  • learning rate \(\eta = 1\)
  • starting weights \(w_i = 1/8\)

You do not have to build the stumps. They are given (they are the best weighted-SSE splits found in each round):

Stump Rule
\(h_1(x)\) \(5.00\) if \(x \le 6.5\), otherwise \(9.50\)
\(h_2(x)\) \(2.00\) if \(x \le 1.5\), otherwise \(6.76\)
\(h_3(x)\) \(3.59\) if \(x \le 4.5\), otherwise \(8.61\)

Recall, for each round \(m\):

\[\bar L_m=\sum_i w_iL_i,\qquad \beta_m=\frac{\bar L_m}{1-\bar L_m},\qquad \alpha_m=\eta\ln\frac1{\beta_m},\qquad w_i^{new}\propto w_i\,\beta_m^{\,\eta(1-L_i)}\]

and the final model \(H(x)\) is the weighted median of \(h_1(x),h_2(x),h_3(x)\) with weights \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3\).

Questions

Q1 (20 pts), Round 1.

  1. Write the starting weights. (b) Compute the predictions of \(h_1\) and the absolute errors \(|y_i-\hat y_i|\). (c) Find \(D_1\) and the loss \(L_i\) of every row. (d) Compute \(\bar L_1\), \(\beta_1\) and \(\alpha_1\). (e) Compute the new weights (before and after normalizing). Which row now has the largest weight?

Q2 (25 pts), Round 2. Repeat Q1 (b) to (e) for \(h_2\), using the weights you found in Q1(e).

Q3 (15 pts), Round 3. For \(h_3\), using the weights from Q2, compute \(D_3\), \(\bar L_3\), \(\beta_3\) and \(\alpha_3\). (You do not need the new weights.)

Q4 (20 pts), Final model.

  1. Write the final model \(H(x)\) in terms of \(h_m\) and \(\alpha_m\).
  2. Compute \(H(2)\) and \(H(7)\), showing the sorted predictions and the cumulative voting power.
  3. Compute \(H(x)\) for all 8 rows and the training MSE. Compare it with the MSE of \(h_1\) alone.

Q5 (10 pts), Plots. Draw (i) three plots, one per stump, with the point size proportional to the weight used to fit that stump, and (ii) one plot of the final model \(H(x)\) on top of the data.

Q6 (10 pts), Concept questions.

  1. Which row has the largest error in Round 1, and what happens to its weight? Why?
  2. A stump has \(\bar L=0.55\). What are \(\beta\) and \(\alpha\)? What should the algorithm do?
  3. Redo \(\alpha_1\) with \(\eta=0.5\), and compute the raw new weight of the row with \(x=2\). What does a smaller \(\eta\) do?
  4. Why does AdaBoost.R2 combine stumps with a weighted median instead of a weighted mean?

Solution

Q1: Round 1

(a) Starting weights: \(w_i = 1/8 = 0.125\) for every row.

(b)–(c) Predictions, errors and losses of \(h_1\):

x y w1 h1(x) |y − ŷ| L
1 2 0.125 5.0 3.0 1.0000
2 5 0.125 5.0 0.0 0.0000
3 5 0.125 5.0 0.0 0.0000
4 5 0.125 5.0 0.0 0.0000
5 7 0.125 5.0 2.0 0.4444
6 6 0.125 5.0 1.0 0.1111
7 10 0.125 9.5 0.5 0.0278
8 9 0.125 9.5 0.5 0.0278

The largest error is \(D_1 = 3.00\) (at \(x=1\)), so that row has \(L=1\) and every other loss is \((|y-\hat y|/3)^2\).

(d)

\[\bar L_1=\sum_i w_iL_i = 0.125\,(1.0000 + 0.4444 + 0.1111 + 0.0278 + 0.0278) = 0.2014\]

\[\beta_1=\frac{0.2014}{1-0.2014}=0.2522 \qquad \alpha_1=\ln\frac{1}{0.2522}=1.378\]

(e) New weights \(w\cdot\beta_1^{\,1-L}\), then divide by the total:

x y w1 L raw w2 w2
1 2 0.125 1.0000 0.1250 0.3290
2 5 0.125 0.0000 0.0315 0.0830
3 5 0.125 0.0000 0.0315 0.0830
4 5 0.125 0.0000 0.0315 0.0830
5 7 0.125 0.4444 0.0581 0.1530
6 6 0.125 0.1111 0.0367 0.0967
7 10 0.125 0.0278 0.0328 0.0862
8 9 0.125 0.0278 0.0328 0.0862

Total of the raw weights \(=0.3799\). The largest weight is now at \(x=1\) (\(w_2=0.3290\)).

Q4: Final model

(a) \(H(x)=\text{weighted median}\{h_1(x),h_2(x),h_3(x)\}\) with weights \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3\).

With the values above: \(\alpha_1=1.378\), \(\alpha_2=1.343\), \(\alpha_3=0.673\) (total \(3.394\), half \(=1.697\)).

(b) Sort the three predictions, add up the voting powers, and stop at the first cumulative value \(\ge\) half the total.

Q6: Concept questions

(a) The largest Round-1 error is at \(x=1\) (\(y=2\), \(h_1=5.0\), error \(3\)), so \(L=1\). Its raw weight is multiplied by \(\beta_1^{0}=1\) while every other row is multiplied by \(\beta_1^{1-L}<1\). After normalizing, its weight rises from \(0.125\) to \(0.329\). Rows that the stump fits badly get more weight, so the next stump focuses on them.

(b) \(\beta=0.55/0.45=1.222>1\), so \(\alpha=\ln(1/\beta)=-0.201<0\). The stump is worse than chance, so the algorithm stops (or discards that stump).

(c) With \(\eta=0.5\): \(\alpha_1=0.5\ln(1/0.2522)=0.689\) (instead of 1.378). The raw weight at \(x=2\) (with \(L=0\)) is \(0.125\cdot0.2522^{0.5}=0.0628\) (instead of 0.0315). A smaller learning rate gives smaller voting powers and gentler weight changes, so more stumps are needed; it learns more slowly but is usually more stable.

(d) A weighted mean can be pulled far away by one stump with a wild prediction (especially one with a big voting power). The weighted median takes the prediction that the majority of the voting power agrees on, so it is robust to a single bad stump.
